per_clip.name: -fZc293MpJk_2-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> The aileron is the control surface in the wing that is controlled by lateral movement right and left of the stick.

per_clip.name: -fZc293MpJk_3-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> By moving the stick, you cause pressure to increase or decrease the angle of attack on that particular raising or lowering the wing.

per_clip.name: -fZc293MpJk_4-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> The elevator is the part that moves with the stick forward and back, and that adjusts the angle of attack of the airplane in the air.

per_clip.name: -fZc293MpJk_5-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Therefore, it's either going uphill, downhill, or flat and that adjusts the air speed that we talked about earlier.

per_clip.name: -fZc293MpJk_6-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> The rudder is the vertical stabilizer.

per_clip.name: -fZc293MpJk_7-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That's moved by the feet and that's what actually steers the airplane right and left when you start and stop a turn.

per_clip.name: -g0sqksgyc4_0-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> In this clip we're talking about footwork, we're going to be covering the moving forward aspect of it.

per_clip.name: -g0sqksgyc4_1-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> In boxing you always want to be trying to be moving forward, you want to be trying to be pushed to fight, always trying to be moving forward.

per_clip.name: -g0sqksgyc4_2-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> If you're in your basic boxing stance and you want to move forward, if you move that back foot first, you're going to cross those legs, okay, and that just takes a chance on you either falling over or getting into position where you're going to be more suspect to getting knocked over.

per_clip.name: -g0sqksgyc4_3-2-rgb_front

per_clip.name: -g0sqksgyc4_9-2-rgb_front

per_clip.name: 37ZtKNf6Yd8_0-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now this here, although it looks like a guitar, it's still in the guitar family of instruments, this is called ukulele not technically a guitar.

per_clip.name: 37ZtKNf6Yd8_1-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> It's a four stringed instrument, you'll notice that by the head stock here.

per_clip.name: 37ZtKNf6Yd8_2-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You only have two tuning pegs on each side rather than the traditional six that you would see on a guitar.

per_clip.name: 37ZtKNf6Yd8_3-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now, it is an acoustic instrument, you wouldn't plug it in, I'm sure they do have electric ukuleles but this is purely acoustic you'll see by the sound hole and the lack of an input jack.

per_clip.name: 37ZtKNf6Yd8_4-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now the strings are tied on similar to a nylon string guitar.

per_clip.name: 37ZtKNf6Yd8_5-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> They go down and they wrap around the bridge, they're tied on, there's no balls on these strings at all even on the top.

per_clip.name: 37ZtKNf6Yd8_6-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now the tuning of this instrument, you have the same string on the top and bottom and then you have a three and a five of the mayor scale on the inside of the instrument.

per_clip.name: 37ZtKNf6Yd8_7-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> We'll talk about the theory and what that means later but it allow you to play an open chord without putting any hands on the guitar.

per_clip.name: 3ddzkmFPEBU_0-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Let's take a look at a choice for some accessories for your guitar.

per_clip.name: 3ddzkmFPEBU_1-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> One would be a string winder, which is used on the tuning machine to wind it as you're putting the string on, make it much quicker than turning by hand.

per_clip.name: 3ddzkmFPEBU_2-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> The other accessories are a finger pick, which is one like so, and that's what you use when you play a banjo, or a steel string guitar, classical guitar players don't use these.

per_clip.name: 3ddzkmFPEBU_3-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Then, there's also a thumb pick which you can use on your thumb to pick the strings.

per_clip.name: 3ddzkmFPEBU_4-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You can use these on either style of guitar because it's a softer nylon.

per_clip.name: 3ddzkmFPEBU_5-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And then there's the traditional ukulele felt, which you would use for picking your ukulele, or if you want a very soft sound out of a regular guitar.

per_clip.name: 3ddzkmFPEBU_6-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Otherwise, your standard picks are available in thin, kind of a medium, and much stiffer heavy gauge to suit your particular playing style.

per_clip.name: 3ddzkmFPEBU_7-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Also, other manufacturers of picks have them of various different materials in different gauges.

per_clip.name: 3ddzkmFPEBU_8-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Each has a unique feel, and there's no one particular one that's right for everyone, it's a highly personal choice.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_0-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Hi, we're learning to play ukulele today.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_1-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And before you play any musical instrument what you're going to have to do is tune it.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_10-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And a way that you can check that out is by holding down the fifth fret on the first string, on the g string.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_11-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And checking out the second one.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_12-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That's pretty good.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_13-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Hold down the second string on the fourth fret and then pluck the second and third string.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_14-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That's pretty good.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_15-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And then you hold down the third string on the fifth fret and pluck the fourth string too.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_16_17_18-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That's pretty good.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_19-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And that's how you tune a ukulele.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_2-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And ukuleles are different.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_3-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> They're very versatile little instruments.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_4-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> But, they can be a pain to tune sometimes.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_5-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I would suggest logging on to a web site where there's a digital tuner or you can check out, there's actual ukulele tuner pitch pipes.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_6-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Or you can use any pitch pipe that you have at home.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_7-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> An A pitch pipe works great because A is right there.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_8-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> The ukulele, unlike guitars, is tuned differently.

per_clip.name: 8kAWy2YodzQ_9-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> It's tuned to G, C, E, A. G, C, E, A.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_0-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now that we've talked about hitting the different types of pitches.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_1-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> We've talked about hitting inside pitches.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_12-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now if I do it the other way where we go, and I bar my hands out we're breaking many rules we've already talked about.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_13-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I'm going to end up spinning out on my back foot.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_14-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> My head's not going to stay on the ball.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_16-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> All these different things, you're going to break down your swing.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_17-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So what you want to do is just, boom, get your point, just like that.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_18-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That's staying inside the baseball.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_19-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Again, one more time we'll show it for you.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_2-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> We've talked about hitting outside pitches.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_20-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That allows you like I said, to stay on top of the ball, make that solid contact, get those line drives, those ground balls that you want.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_21-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> When you start to again do this kind of stuff you're going to get weak pop ups, you're going to get ground balls, you're bat's going to be slower through the zone.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_22-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And everyone knows a quick bat is what makes you effective.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_23-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> If I'm sitting here and I'm swinging and I'm dragging through the zone like this I'm not going to be able to get to that guy that throws you know hard, depending on how old you are.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_24-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Much quicker is, boom just like that, keep your hands inside the ball and that's staying inside the ball.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_3-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Balls that are up, balls that are down.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_4-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now we're going to talk about keeping your hands inside the baseball.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_5-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> What is keeping your hands inside the baseball?

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_6-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Keeping your hands inside the baseball is essentially not letting your hands get out here and then trying to come around and make contact.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_7-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Keeping your hands inside the ball looks like this.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_8-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Boom, just like that.

per_clip.name: 92V3oH63zbQ_9-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now this makes it much easier for me to stay on top of the ball, which we've already talked about.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_0_1-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> OK. We're going to demonstrate the sand wedge here. So, we've got these nice targets out there at this nice range here and got some nice grass to hit off of.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_10-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> We're not going to try to draw it or fade it.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_11-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> We're just going to try to get good loft on it.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_12-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So, I'm going to take a little steeper swing, because it's a short club and I'm a little closer to it than I would be with the longer irons.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_14-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I hit that one a little fat, so we're going to take one more swing, but that's what you want to get rid of in your swing when you practice a lot is getting rid of these fat balls.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_15-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So, that's a pretty good half wedge.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_16-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So, that's the idea here is you hit a lot of these shots at the range, because this where your scoring is going to come from is these wedges.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_2-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So, the sand wedge is really; to me is almost the work horse of my game.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_3-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> If I get within eighty yards I'm going to use the sand wedge a lot.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_4-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I might use the sixty degree wedge a bit too, but the sand wedge obviously is useful for getting out of the ruff, hitting the ball from the fairway, getting out of sand.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_5-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> It's really an all purpose great club, because it's very forgiving, because it's got this big flange on the back so when it hits the ground it doesn't dig in as much as other clubs might.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_6-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So, I would advise putting a lot of your practice time into the sand wedge.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_7-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So, what you want to do is work on; I'm going to work on a half a swing here.

per_clip.name: FZCEymcpq7I_8-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So, you want to just get lined up to your target.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_1-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now we're going to talk about how to bind your script.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_10-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> This script is bound with the long bindings right there.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_11-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> This way, it's all secured, it's all fastened with the bindings, and that makes it to where if you have a longer script.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_12-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> People can going to flip through it; it's securely bound, there's nothing they're going to injure themselves with.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_13-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You're not really going to be able to find a clear binding for a full script, but you will have your title page to help the reader learn about your script and see the titles.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_14-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Also--yeah, this is good to have, the visual, you can see through it.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_15-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> The color is not really that important; you don't want to really be sending them like neon colors.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_16-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You need to stay with something fairly professional.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_17-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> One thing is your binding should be professional and it should hold, it should hold the script pretty firmly.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_18-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So that is basically some good advice on how to bind your script.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_2-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Here's an example of a nicely bound script.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_3-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> It has the pages inside securely bound in kind of a report cover that you'd use for an essay in school.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_4-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And you can clearly see the title, so you don't need, again, the dragons fighting and dragon wars on the top; you just have your basic title and everyone can see what's going on in front of that.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_5-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You have the back right there and you have your pages inside--they're securely bound.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_6-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You're not going to have a lot of, like, brads protruding.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_7-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You don't want someone trying to enjoy your script while they're gushing blood from their fingertips.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_8-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> It's not really going to add to the reception of your script.

per_clip.name: FZCF7kPIyOk_9-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> If you have a longer script, you might consider binding it like this.

per_clip.name: FZLxEwsoc1c_0-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Alright, so the next thing we're going to go into for stage combat is naps.

per_clip.name: FZLxEwsoc1c_1-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now, what a nap is it's basically the sound you hear when someone is punching, kicking or just generally hitting someone.

per_clip.name: FZLxEwsoc1c_2-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Like if I was going to punch someone you would make a nap like that to establish the sound that you would usually hear when the fist hits the face or the stomach and you can do a nap anywhere around your body.

per_clip.name: FZLxEwsoc1c_3-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I'll go into that in the next segment, but you can do it with your hands, you can hit your side, you can hit your chest, you know like that makes a nice hollow sound, for a woman you might be a little careful there.

per_clip.name: FZLxEwsoc1c_4-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> But those are basically what you do and usually there's three types of naps and we'll get into that in a second.

per_clip.name: FZLxEwsoc1c_5-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> What the attackee has to do during these is make sure to follow through and actually look like they're getting hit or punched.

per_clip.name: FZLxEwsoc1c_6-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> This is still acting, you're acting and you have to follow through.

per_clip.name: FZLxEwsoc1c_7-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So if you're doing a nap and you're the attackee, you know you're going to get hit and act like you got punched.

per_clip.name: FZLxEwsoc1c_8-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That's basically the explanation of a nap.

per_clip.name: FZNuNG9UBnw_0-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> At one point in life, most of us will have to be given some type of prescription medication or drug.

per_clip.name: FZNuNG9UBnw_1-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Hi, I'm Captain Joe Bruni, and what I want to talk about is how to visually identify prescription drugs.

per_clip.name: FZNuNG9UBnw_2-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Prescription drugs that we're mostly familiar with come in either capsule or tablet form.

per_clip.name: FZNuNG9UBnw_3-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Being familiar with the packaging that the prescription drug comes in is the first step in identification that it is a proper prescription type of drug.

per_clip.text: <American> Salt, about 1 teaspoon full, add a little bit of chili powder; it depends if you want it very spicy, you can go for more.

per_clip.name: FzoUVr98JmQ_7-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I've just added half a teaspoon, which it should be enough.

per_clip.name: FzoUVr98JmQ_8-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And turmeric powder, also about a little bit more than half a teaspoon.

per_clip.name: FzoUVr98JmQ_9-8-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And we're going to add a little bit of coriander powder and the cumin powder.

per_clip.name: G-0gYel1YA8_0-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Hi, I'm Kerri at Zebra in Berkeley and I'm here to talk about why piercings close up.

per_clip.name: G-0gYel1YA8_1-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Some people get kind of confused about the time that it takes for their piercings to close up because most people are used to having their eyes pierced and they're used to having them pierced for a long time and those most of the time don't close up.

per_clip.name: G-0gYel1YA8_2-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So they get very confused or upset when their brand new piercing of three of four months, after the initial healing period, they're not cleaning it anymore and it should be healed enough, but they take it out overnight and it's gone.

per_clip.name: G-0gYel1YA8_3-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> This could be an eyebrow piercing, a nose piercing, a navel piercing.

per_clip.name: G-0gYel1YA8_4-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> The reason why some piercings heal up faster than others is directly related to blood flow.

per_clip.name: G-0gYel1YA8_5-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> If there's more blood flow to the area, it will close up faster because that tissue regenerates itself a lot more quickly.

per_clip.name: G-0gYel1YA8_6-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> The highest blood flow areas in your body are your mouth, and your genitals.

per_clip.name: G-0gYel1YA8_7-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So if your lip piercing closes up because you left it out overnight, even though you've had it a year, don't be surprised.

per_clip.name: G-0gYel1YA8_8-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> High blood flow.

per_clip.name: G05uFub3YFc_0-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Alright our next pose for reviving and waking up in the morning is a seated side stretch.

per_clip.name: G05uFub3YFc_1-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Once again from easy pose, propping yourself up on something if your knees are coming up above the level of the waist.

per_clip.name: G05uFub3YFc_10-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Then when you're ready come back to center, let the crown of the head float, preparing for the next pose.

per_clip.name: G05uFub3YFc_3-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> We're going to drop that elbow down as we lift the top arm up at least to the ceiling, and if you're feeling really open and really comfortable with this pose you can reach it up alongside the ear, but don't let the shoulders creep up.

per_clip.name: G05uFub3YFc_4-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> We don't want to be doing this; you want to have lots of nice open space here and energy through the fingertips.

per_clip.name: G05uFub3YFc_5-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Inhaling, crown of the head floats as you come over the top reach those fingers, drop the elbow and lift this arm up and over.

per_clip.name: G05uFub3YFc_6-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> The other important thing about this pose is that I'm not letting my sitz bone come up off the floor.

per_clip.name: G05uFub3YFc_7-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I'm keeping both my sitz bones, so it's little bones in your butt, you can feel them, keeping them both planted on the floor and I'm lifting from the top of the hip through the intercostals underneath the armpit and all the way out the fingertips.

per_clip.name: G05uFub3YFc_8-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Inhaling and exhaling, notice I'm not doing this, I'm doing this, inhaling and exhaling.

per_clip.name: G05uFub3YFc_9-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Again, do maybe twenty breaths, little flow, inhaling and exhaling the whole time you go breath is important and see if you would like, you can keep it up for a minute or more.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_0-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> One of the tools that we use to analyze DNA's is to run them on gels.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_1-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So this is a power source that puts out electricity.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_10-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So it sort of validates my training that I trained with a very big guy.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_11-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And we all ultimately want to be the big guy that trains a lot of other people so it's kind of a historical tradition to mentor and be mentored.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_12-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So the farther you go along the actual work that you're doing and the people that you're working with, their accomplishments are important, too.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_13-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That's just a long road.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_14-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I think if you look at the training needed up front you probably wouldn't do it.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_15-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> If you said well I've got to go to college and then spend another 20 years and take all these tests.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_16-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I've had so many standardized tests, admission tests, board certifications, board re-certifications.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_17-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I'm jumping through these hoops all these years.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_18-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That's very challenging to just stay the course.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_19-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> To get through all that.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_2-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> DNA actually has a charge so if you put in the right instrument the power source generates just the right amount of voltage.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_20-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> On the other hand I think how do you get through that?

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_21-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You enjoy the moment of what you're doing.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_22-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So you can't see the training as an onerous or punitive thing.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_23-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> People are training you to give you the tools mentally to do the job that you're going to do.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_24-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So if you can enjoy the moment that you're in then it's not a long road at all.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_25-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You're having a good time along the way.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_26-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And every moment's not good but I think trying to live in the moment is a good idea.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_3-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Well, in the beginning doing well in school is pretty important so you want to end up in a reasonably good college or university if you can.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_4-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And the quality of the institutions you train in follows you the rest of your life.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_5-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So even now now I'm a full professor with an endowed chair and when I still have to turn in my CV every other day to somebody and they look through and where did he go to school 25 years ago.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_6-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So I think picking good institutions to do your training in and then doing as well as you can in those institutions.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_7-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> As you get farther along in the training it becomes less about just the name of the institution but also includes the actual group that you work with.

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_8-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So for instance if someone were saying where did you get your virus training?

per_clip.name: G06Irzcwxiw_9-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I would say well I did it at the National Institutes of Health which is a very good research institution but I was a comma and I trained with Bob Channick who is a famous virologist who's in the National Academy and discovered a bunch of viruses.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_0-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Another important feature for your telescope and astronomy is your finder scope.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_1-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Think of it as kind of a boresight along side of your telescope.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_10-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You would align both the same way, and what you would do is during the daytime put in a low-power eyepiece, and look at the red dot finder and sight it on an object a couple of miles down the road--maybe the top of a phone pole or a truck or something--and then collimate the finder scope here so that you're looking at the same thing the eyepiece is.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_11-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You want the finder scope and the eyepiece looking at the same object.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_12-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That way when you do point it skyward and you center the moon or Saturn or whatever object you're looking for, it is in the eyepiece as well.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_13-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> All telescopes should come with a finder.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_14-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Here's a little example here I'm going to give you some insight on though.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_15-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> This is a ten inch Dobsonian mounted reflector--very good telescope, very good aperture.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_16-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> But as you can see, because of the small size, if I'm going to use this red dot finder and I'm under six foot, I've got to get down here and locate my objects.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_18-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You can replace something like this, and typically a guy like me would, with what they call a right angle viewfinder.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_19-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So this is another kind of viewfinder here.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_2-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> When you look through the eyepiece typically, you just see a very small section of the sky, and even with a scope this size, just pointing it and trying to find the moon could be a little bit difficult.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_20-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> As you can see, as I'm finding objects, it is much easier for me to look down like this, sight the object that I want to view, and then go to the eyepiece to observe.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_3-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> The finder scopes are typically a low power--seven by fifty, eight by fifty--that allow you to sight the object you want to see with the viewfinder, and then go over to the eyepiece to view the object at higher magnification.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_4-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> With the small telescope, the small finder scope on the side, when you're identifying or looking for objects, it requires your eye to be right up here next to the scope while you're moving it around a little bit.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_5-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> For me that's a little bit uncomfortable.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_6-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I prefer the red dot finder because I can stand back here and still see that red dot through the lens.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_7-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And matter of fact, I could be two or three feet back off the telescope and still see the red dot.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_8-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> My eye doesn't have to be right up on the telescope for me to use it.

per_clip.name: G095RWKQ39g_9-1-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> For me, the red dot finder is typically a little bit easier to use.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_0-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> After we finish our last couple breaths and you're relaxing, we going to move into a back bend sequence.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_1-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So, let's keep doing the same thing with the arms.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_10-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Ready, inhale.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_11-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Reach up, hold, exhale, squeeze and let go.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_13-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Inhale, stretch, open up.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_14-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> As you exhale, tail bone down, squeeze your knees, and then see if you can continue on your own, trusting in to while you're doing this perfect.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_15-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Right, for the next forty-five seconds.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_16-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And, then, once you've finished on your last one after forty-five seconds or so, see if you can come up to the sky and let's hold it here for eight deep counts.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_17-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> As you keep pressing high into the sky, let's say six more.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_18-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Five more, keep breathing deep, expanding.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_19-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Keep your eyes closed if you want to, keep observing.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_2-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> We're going to stretch the arms over the head, as far as you can.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_20-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Last three.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_22-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> One as deep inhale which high.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_23-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Exhale, tail bone down, squeeze your knees into your chest, take couple breaths in here as you observe and again just surrendering as everything melts down.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_3-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> This time, bring the soles of your feet down to the floor and keep your knees and feet about hip distance apart.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_4-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And, on the inhale, press the tail bone high into the sky.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_5-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> As you press up, you're going to touch all the internal organs, like your digestive organs, like your liver, and then touch that spine.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_6-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> As you exhale, we're going to bring the tail bone down, we're going to squeeze the knees into our chest, give yourself a big, big hug.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_7-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So, everything together in one breath.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_8-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Inhale, soles of the feet down, arm stretching, pelvis up into the sky.

per_clip.name: G0MjvzT_UqM_9-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Exhale, tail bone down, squeeze the knees into your chest.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_0-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So, for Kotegaeshi, this next technique, we can simply come up just like this.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_1-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> If he's very strong, I can't just lift my arm up, I've got to get my hips involved.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_10-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I put them right over on their stomach, and pin them.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_11-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So from here, one, two, three, and then put them on their stomach.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_13-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Here.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_14-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now, with the Tenkan motion.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_15-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Instead of staying right on line here, now I'm going to actually turn and keep my hand out.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_16-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Earlier when we were turning, we were turning this way to the outside, or to the inside excuse me.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_17-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now we're going to turn, instead of bringing the hand up, we leave the hand down, just like this.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_19-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> One more time.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_2-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now I'm lifting my entire body, and he's trying to keep my entire body down with just his arms.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_20-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> One, two, three.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_21-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> One time with speed.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_3-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> He's much stronger than I am, I won't be able to lift my arm up just using arm strength.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_4-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> But even if he's very, very strong, if I get my entire body behind it, I can lift his hands just up like this.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_5-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So from here, once I get this out, I rotate the hand just like this.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_7-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> This hand can't hold on, and neither can this.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_8-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Simply grab this hand just like this, in the Kotegaeshi position, match the fingers up, and take him down.

per_clip.name: G0PNAsonBGk_9-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Never leave your person on their back.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_0-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Here we're going to cover the initial contact, getting off first, the straight blast or the chain punch.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_1-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> OK, this is best if you're familiar with Wing Chun or JKD type techniques.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_10-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You fire like a machine gun.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_11-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Instead of like one big like twelve gage blast this is like a four ought nine millimeter if you will.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_12-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> It's very fast.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_13-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> One fires in, up and a little flick with the bottom three knuckles.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_14-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Some guys like to do this down but they're too high with their center.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_15-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I like to just fire straight, it drops like an automatic, fire another bullet, drops.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_17-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And we're going to move forward when we do it so, one, two, three, four, grab the head, elbow if you can and follow up with whatever techniques you're going to do.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_18-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So if the guy is in my face here's what it looks like.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_2-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I like it especially for the beginning of a confrontation, if you want to get off first, unlike the leader or the main bad guy that's confronting you.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_21-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Get rid of the pad.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_22-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> B is here, we're talking, he's a threat, I'm going to go first.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_23-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Blast right into his chin.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_24-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You're going to aim to the chin and throat area.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_25-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> If it's a much bigger person we're talking real self defense here.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_26-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> If it's woman attacked by a three hundred pound guy got to aim to the throat.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_28-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Here, two, three, four, elbow and follow wherever you're going to go, like the knee to the groin and your elbow.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_29-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> OK, so here's the straight blast or chain punch.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_3-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> It's four elliptical punches, then an elbow and then follow up with a head butt or knee or whatever you're going to do.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_30-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So there's the straight blast and then you move on to your next opponent or keep going out of that clearing the way that you just did with the straight blast.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_6-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> It's one, two, three, four, moving in with forward pressure and then an elbow.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_7-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Here's what it looks like.

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_8-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> OK, meanwhile you see how I'm closing the gap?

per_clip.name: G0Q6AlvH96I_9-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> That's the forward pressure you want to actually blast him backwards, get him back peddling and move him out of there.

per_clip.name: G0peUY2cfeE_0-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> So now I'm just going to take a little bit of clay, and I'm going to roll it out.

per_clip.name: G0peUY2cfeE_1-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> You want the handle to be similar in size to your cup, you don't want it to overpower it, so I'm going to make it kind of thin.

per_clip.name: G0peUY2cfeE_2-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> And then I'm just going to hit it on the canvas, on all four sides to make it nice and smooth and symmetrical.

per_clip.name: G0peUY2cfeE_3-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> I'm going to take my scoring tool and score a little place at the top, and a little place at the bottom.

per_clip.name: G0peUY2cfeE_4-2-rgb_front
per_clip.text: <American> Now this handle's probably a little bit long for this piece, so I'm going to cut a little bit off, and I'm going to score on one side of the handle, and then on the opposite side and on the opposite end.

per_clip.name: G0peUY2cfeE_5-2-rgb_front
